options: Letting attacker-controlled input change a query's structure, not just the value being filtered on
A governor limit violation caused by too many SOQL queries
A syntax error caused by a missing bind variable
A type of semi-join that returns unexpected results
questions.explain: SOQL injection happens when untrusted input breaks out of its intended value and adds or alters the query's own logic/structure.

questions.q: Why does a bind variable (e.g. WHERE Industry = :filterValue) prevent injection, while string concatenation does not?
options: Bind variables only work with numeric fields, so injection via text is impossible
Bind variables automatically remove all special characters from user input
The bind variable's value is always passed as data, never spliced into the query text as additional syntax
Bind variables disable the WHERE clause entirely
questions.explain: A bind variable passes the value purely as data for comparison — it can never be interpreted as additional query syntax, unlike a concatenated string.

questions.q: What does Database.queryWithBinds provide that Database.query alone does not?
options: Automatic conversion of SOQL into SOSL
A safe way to pass bind variable values into a dynamic SOQL query string via a separate map
A way to bypass governor limits
Built-in pagination with no OFFSET limit
questions.explain: queryWithBinds takes the dynamic query string plus a separate map of bind values, keeping user-supplied values out of the concatenated query text.

questions.q: According to Salesforce's own guidance, how should String.escapeSingleQuotes() be regarded?
options: As a replacement for field-level security checks
As the strongest and preferred defense against all forms of SOQL injection
As unnecessary once governor limits are enforced
As a narrower fallback for simple string comparisons, weaker than bind variables, not a complete injection defense on its own
questions.explain: Salesforce documents escapeSingleQuotes() as a fallback for simple cases, noting not every injection technique requires a single quote and that it should be combined with other validation.

questions.q: If a feature must let a user choose which field to filter a dynamic query on, what should happen to that input before it reaches the query string?
options: It should be validated against an explicit allow-list of real, permitted field names
It should be passed directly as a bind variable with no further checks
It should be wrapped in String.escapeSingleQuotes() only
Field names never need validation since they can't be used for injection
questions.explain: Bind variables protect WHERE clause values, but field/object names are structural parts of the query — Salesforce's guidance is to validate these against an allow-list rather than trust user input directly.
